rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bathth is the most unbearable anxiety, which its sufferer therefore broadcasts; Jacob says he complains only to God, seeking Him and taking refuge in Him.
rows.anchor: البث أصعب الهم الذي لا يصبر عليه صاحبه فيبثه إلى الناس أي ينشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divine revelation reportedly explains Jacob's distress as punishment for slaughtering a sheep while a poor person stood at his door and received no food; prophets and then the poor are God's most beloved creatures, so Jacob should feed the poor.
rows.anchor: إنما وجدت عليكم لأنكم ذبحتم شاة فوقفت بباكم مسكين فلم تطعموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Jacob bought an enslaved woman with her child, sold the child, and her weeping continued until she became blind.
rows.anchor: اشترى جارية مع ولدها فباع ولدها فبكت حتى عميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knows from God's mercy that relief will come to him unexpectedly.
rows.anchor: وأعلم من رحمته أنه يأيتني بالفرج من حيث لا احتسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a dream Jacob asked the Angel of Death whether Joseph had died; told Joseph was alive, he was to seek him and use a prayer asking the Ever-Beneficent to relieve him.
rows.anchor: رأى ملك الموت في منامه فسأله هل قبضت روح يوسف فقال لا والله هو حى فاطلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥassasū means seek information and identify Joseph and his brother; it derives from iḥsās, awareness or recognition.
rows.anchor: فتعرفوا منهما وتطلبوا خبرهما وهو تفعل من الإحساس وهو المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rūḥ Allāh means God's mercy and relief; believers do not despair because they know they move within His mercy and favor, whereas disbelievers do not know this.
rows.anchor: ولا تقنطوا من رحمة الله وفرجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's sons leave him and return to Egypt to search for Joseph and his brother.
rows.anchor: فخرجوا من عند أبيهم راجعين إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harm that touched the family means emaciation from hardship and hunger.
rows.anchor: مسنا وأهلنا الضر ﴾ الهزال من الشدة والجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rejected, depreciated commodity is one merchants push away; the term derives from pushing or driving something off.
rows.anchor: مدفوعة يدفعها كل تاجر رغبة عنها واحتقارا لها من أزجيته إذا دفعته وطردته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says their poor payment consisted of debased dirhams accepted only at a discount.
rows.anchor: قيل كانت دراهم زيوفا لا تؤخذ إلا بوضيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says their poor payment consisted of wool and clarified butter.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانت صوفا وسمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask Joseph to give them the full measure that is their due.
rows.anchor: فأوف لنا الكيل ﴾ الذي هو حقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request to be treated charitably can mean overlooking the poor quality of their goods, adding to their due, or giving them their brother.
rows.anchor: وتفضل علينا بالمسامحة والإغماض عن رداءة البضاعة أو زدنا على حقنا أو هب لنا أخانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards those who give charity.
rows.anchor: إن الله يجزي المتصدقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they described their hardship and pleaded for charity, Joseph's eyes overflowed and he could not restrain himself from revealing his identity.
rows.anchor: تضرعوا إليه وطلبوا منه أن يتصدق عليهم ارفضت عيناه ولم يتمالك أن عرفهم نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks whether they now recognize how vile their treatment of him was.
rows.anchor: هل علمتم قبح ما فعلتم بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' earlier ignorance may mean they did not recognize the wickedness of their act, or that they were immature, foolish, and rash.
rows.anchor: لا تعلمون قبحه أو إذ أنتم في حد السفه والطيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their treatment of Benjamin exposed him to grief by separating him from his full brother, and they harmed him in many ways.
rows.anchor: تعرضهم إياه للغم بإفراده عن أخيه لأبيه وأمه وإيذاؤهم له بانواع الاذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They acknowledge that God preferred Joseph over them through knowledge, forbearance, piety, patience, and beauty.
rows.anchor: اختارك وفضلك علينا بالعلم والحلم والتقوى والصبر والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confession means they had deliberately sinned, neither practicing piety nor patience.
rows.anchor: أنا كنا خاطئين متعمدين للاثم لم نتق ولم نصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's kingship and their abasement as suppliants before him are the consequences of their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: لا جرم أن الله أعزك بالملك وأذلنا بالتمسكن بين يديك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathrīb means reproach or blame; Joseph's expression can link “today” either to reproach or to God's forgiveness.
rows.anchor: لا تعيير عليكم ﴿ اليوم ﴾ متعلق بالتثريب أو بيغفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning may be that there is no blame today, the day most suited to blame; this implies still more that there is none on other days.
rows.anchor: وهو اليوم الذي هو مظنة التثريب فما ظنكم بغيره من الأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Joseph begins a new sentence with a prayer that God forgive what they did; the past and present forms of the forgiveness formula are both used.
rows.anchor: ثم ابتدأ فقال ﴿ يغفر الله لكم ﴾ فدعا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Today God forgives you” can be understood as glad tidings of forgiveness arriving soon.
rows.anchor: اليوم يغفر الله لكم بشارة بعاجل غفران الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet asked Quraysh what they thought he would do; they expected kindness from a noble kinsman, and he answered with Joseph's words, “No reproach upon you today.”
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ بعضادتى باب الكعبة يوم الفتح

rows.speaker: العباس
rows.claim: When Abu Sufyan came to become Muslim, al-Abbas told him to recite Joseph's words to the Prophet; the Prophet then prayed that God forgive Abu Sufyan and the person who taught him.
rows.anchor: أن أبا سفيان لما جاء ليسلم قال له العباس إذا أتيت رسول الله فاتل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers reportedly felt ashamed to accept Joseph's daily hospitality after their past actions; he said his Egyptian subjects had once seen him as a slave sold for twenty dirhams, but now his honor came through being known as Abraham's descendants.
rows.anchor: إنك تدعونا إلى طعامك بكرة وعشيا ونحن نستحى منك لما فرط منا فيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph reasons that if he, a poor and miserly person, is merciful to them, they should consider how much more merciful the rich, forgiving God is.
rows.anchor: إذا رحمتكم وأنا الفقير القتور فما ظنكم بالغنى الغفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob had become blind from excessive weeping.
rows.anchor: فقالوا أنه عمى من كثرة البكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report identifies Joseph's shirt as an inherited garment kept in his amulet, from Paradise; Gabriel instructed him to send it, and its paradisal scent healed anyone ill or afflicted when it was placed on them.
rows.anchor: القميص المتوارث الذي كان في تعويذ يوسف وكان من الجنة أمره جبريل أن يرسله اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about Jacob becoming seeing can mean he became able to see, or that Joseph would come to him while he was seeing.
rows.anchor: يصر بصيرا تقول جاء البناء محكما أي صار أو يأت إلى وهو بصير

rows.speaker: يهوذا
rows.claim: Judah said he would carry the healing shirt, just as he had previously carried the shirt of estrangement.
rows.anchor: قال يهوذا أما احمل قميص الشفاء كما ذهبت بقميص الجفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said Judah carried the shirt barefoot and bareheaded from Egypt to Canaan, a distance of eighty farsakhs.
rows.anchor: حمله وهو حاف حاسر من مصر إلى كنعان وبينهما مسيرة ثمانين فرسخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks that the whole family come so they may enjoy the effects of his kingship, just as they suffered from reports of his losses.
rows.anchor: لينعموا بآثار ملكى كما اغتموا بأخبار هلكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are Joseph's descendants, and they say Jacob remains in an old error or departure from sound judgment.
rows.anchor: في ذهابك عن الصواب قديما في إفراط محبتك ليوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their accusation may refer to Jacob's excessive love for Joseph or to his old mistake of loving Joseph, whom they believed dead.
rows.anchor: في إفراط محبتك ليوسف أو في خطئك القديم من حب يوسف وكان عندهم انه قد مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bearer of good news is Judah.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فلما أن جاء البشير ﴾ اي يهوذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “he cast it upon his face” may mean the bearer cast the shirt on Jacob's face or Jacob cast it on himself.
rows.anchor: طرح البشير القميص على وجه يعقوب أو ألفاه يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irtaadda means returned; the verb can be formed as raddahu fa-irtaddahu, “he returned it.”
rows.anchor: يقال رده فارتده وارتده اذا ارتجعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's reminder that he had told them may refer to his sensing Joseph's scent or to his instruction not to despair of God's relief.
rows.anchor: يعنى قوله انى لأجد ريح يوسف أو قوله ولا تيأسوا من روح الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the statement about knowing what others do not know may resume Jacob's earlier claim that he complains only to God and knows what others do not.
rows.anchor: والمراد قوله انما أشكو بثى وحزنى إلى الله واعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob asked the bearer about Joseph; on hearing he was Egypt's king, Jacob asked his religion, and the answer that Joseph followed Islam completed the blessing.
rows.anchor: سأل البشير كيف يوسف قال هو ملك مصر فقال ما أصنع بالملك على اي دين تركته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers ask Jacob to seek God's forgiveness for the wrong they committed against him and his son, admitting their sins and repenting.
rows.anchor: سل الله مغفرة ما ارتكبنا في حقك وحق ابنك انا تبنا واعترفنا بخطايانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob delayed seeking forgiveness until the late hours before dawn.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال سوف أستغفر لكم ربي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم ﴾ اخر الاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says he delayed until Friday night.
rows.anchor: أو إلى ليلة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says he waited to learn whether their repentance was sincere.
rows.anchor: أو ليتعرف حالهم في صدق التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says he waited to ask Joseph whether he had pardoned them.
rows.anchor: أو إلى أن يسأل يوسف هل عفا عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph sent his father supplies and two hundred camels so the group could prepare to travel to him.
rows.anchor: وجه إلى أبيه جهازا ومائتى راحلة ليتجهز اليه بمن معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Jacob neared Egypt, Joseph and the king went out with four thousand troops, dignitaries, and all the Egyptians to meet him; Judah supported Jacob as he walked.
rows.anchor: خرج يوسف والملك في أربعة آلاف من الجند والعظماء وأهل مصر بأجمعهم فتلقوا يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Jacob's wife, Joseph's mother, was still alive; another says she had died and Jacob married her sister, who counted as a mother just as an uncle counts as a father.
rows.anchor: قيل كانت أمه باقية وقيل ماتت وتزوج أبوه خالته والخالة أم كما أن العم أب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary cites “the God of your fathers Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac” as an example of calling an uncle a father.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله وإله آبائك إبراهيم واسماعيل واسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family entered Joseph's presence before entering Egypt because he met them and lodged them in a tent or palace there, then embraced his parents.
rows.anchor: معنى دخولهم عليه قبل دخولهم مصر انه حين استقبلهم أنزلهم في مضرب خيمة أو قصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Enter Egypt safely” means safe from its rulers, who otherwise required a guarantee for entry, or safe from famine.
rows.anchor: من ملوكها وكانوا لا يدخلونها الا بجوار أو من القحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At their meeting, Jacob greeted Joseph as the one who dispels sorrows; Joseph wondered why Jacob wept until he lost his sight when they would reunite at the Resurrection, and Jacob feared Joseph might lose his faith and be separated from him.
rows.anchor: السلام عليك يا مذهب الأحزان وقال له يوسف يا أبت بكيت علي حتى ذهب بصرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report counts Jacob's family entering Egypt as seventy-two men and women, while their descendants left with Moses as 600,575 fighting men, besides children and elderly people; the children numbered 1,200,000.
rows.anchor: دخلوا مصر وهم اثنان وسبعون ما بين رجال ونساء وخرجوا منها مع موسى ومقاتلتهم ستمائة ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says the family sat in Joseph's council while he sat on his throne and he honored his parents by raising them onto it; the eleven brothers and both parents then prostrated.
rows.anchor: أكرم أبويه فرفعهما على السرير وخروا له يعنى الإخوة الأحد عشرة والأبوين سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration may have been a customary greeting and honor, comparable to standing, handshaking, or kissing the hand; al-Zajjaj says this was the custom for honoring someone at that time.
rows.anchor: وكانت السجدة عندهم جارية مجرى التحية والتكرمة كالقيام والمصافحة وتقبيل اليد وقال الزجاج سنة التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion that the prostration was only a bow without placing foreheads on the ground is contradicted by the wording that they fell prostrate.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما كانت الا انحناءة دون تعفير الجباه وخرورهم سجدا يأباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they prostrated to God in gratitude for Joseph; this also implies prophethood, though whether Joseph's brothers were prophets is disputed.
rows.anchor: وخروا لأجل يوسف سجدا لله شكرا وفيه نبوة أيضا واختلف في استنبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's earlier dream was true and is now fulfilled.
rows.anchor: أي الرؤيا ﴿ ربي حقا ﴾ اى صادقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interval between Joseph's dream and its interpretation is variously reported as forty, eighty, thirty-six, or twenty-two years.
rows.anchor: وكان بين الرؤيا وبين التأويل اربعون سنة أو ثمانون أو ست وثلاثون أو اثنتان وعشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsana bī is idiomatic alongside aḥsana ilayhi, just as asāʾa bihi is idiomatic alongside asāʾa ilayhi.
rows.anchor: يقال احسن اليه وبه كذلك أساء إليه وبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph does not mention being brought out of the pit, in keeping with his earlier assurance that there would be no reproach.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر الجب لقوله لا تثريب عليكم اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His family came from the open countryside because they herded livestock and moved among water sources and pastures.
rows.anchor: من البادية لأنهم كانوا أصحاب مواش ينتقلون في المياه والمناجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan caused discord and incited hostility between Joseph and his brothers.
rows.anchor: أي أفسد بيننا وأغرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's subtle kindness is subtle management of what He wills; He delayed hopes until their appointed times or decreed reconciliation after discord.
rows.anchor: أي لطيف التدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close of the verse can describe God as delaying hopes to their appointed times, or as decreeing harmony after disagreement.
rows.anchor: بتأخير الآمال إلى الآجال أو حكم بالائتلاف بعد الاختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kingship Joseph received is the kingship of Egypt; his knowledge of interpreting reports means interpreting scripture or dreams, and “of” is partitive because he received only part of worldly kingship and interpretation.
rows.anchor: تفسير كتب الله أو تعبير الرؤيا ومن فيهما للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Originator of the heavens and earth” is in the accusative as a vocative.
rows.anchor: فاطر السماوات والأرض ﴾ انتصابه على النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is Joseph's guardian through blessings in both lives, joining his transient worldly sovereignty to the eternal kingdom.
rows.anchor: أنت الذي تتولانى بالنعمة في الدارين وبوصل الملك الفاني بالملك الباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to die while remaining Muslim, paralleling Jacob's instruction to his sons not to die except as Muslims.
rows.anchor: طلب الوفاة على حال الإسلام كقول يعقوب لولده ولا تموتن الا وأنتم مسلمون

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains “Muslim” here as sincerely devoted.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك مخلصا

rows.speaker: التستري
rows.claim: Al-Tustari explains “Muslim” as having surrendered his affairs to God.
rows.anchor: وعن التسترى مسلما إليك أمرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph prays this way to model it for his people and later people whose final state is uncertain; prophets' outward conduct guides their communities.
rows.anchor: دعا به يوسف ليقتدى به قومه ومن بعده ممن ليس بمأمون العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Join me with the righteous” may mean Joseph's forefathers or the righteous generally.
rows.anchor: من آبائى أو على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph showed Jacob the treasuries; Jacob asked why he had not written during the eight stages between them, and Joseph said Gabriel had forbidden it because of Jacob's fear of the wolf, to which Gabriel answered that Jacob should have feared God.
rows.anchor: قال يا بنى ما اعقك عندك هذه القراطيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Jacob lived with Joseph for twenty-four years, then was buried in Syria beside Isaac at his own request; Joseph accompanied the burial, returned to Egypt, and lived twenty-three years after his father.
rows.anchor: أقام معه أربعا وعشرين سنة ثم مات وأوصى ان يدفنه بالشام إلى جنب أبيه اسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After his affairs were complete, Joseph longed for the everlasting kingdom and wished for death; one view says no prophet before or after him wished for it, and God took him pure.
rows.anchor: فلما تم أمره طلبت نفسه الملك الدائم فتمنى الموت وقيل ما تمناه نبي قبله ولا بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptians disputed over where to bury Joseph and nearly fought; they placed him in a marble coffin in the Nile so its water would pass through Egypt, and Moses moved the coffin to Jerusalem four hundred years later.
rows.anchor: فرأوا ان يعملوا له صندوقا من مرمر وجعلوه فيه ودفنوه في النيل بمكان يمر عليه الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's descendants included Ephraim and Misha; Ephraim's son was Nun, whose son Joshua served Moses; Amalekite Pharaohs inherited Egypt, and Israelites remained under them retaining Joseph's ancestral religion.
rows.anchor: وولدا له افراثيم وميشا وولد لافراثيم نون ولنون يوشع فتى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to the preceding account of Joseph; the address is to Muhammad, and the phrase is parsed as a subject with two predicates.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما سبق من نبأ يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With them” means with the sons of Jacob; they resolved to cast Joseph into the well and plotted against him.
rows.anchor: عزموا على ما هموا به من القاء يوسف في البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is unseen knowledge available to Muhammad only through revelation, since he was not present when Jacob's sons agreed to throw Joseph into the well.
rows.anchor: أن هذا النبأ غيب لم يحصل لك إلا من جهة الوحى لأنك لم تحضر بنى يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers were plotting against Joseph and seeking ways to harm him.
rows.anchor: يمكرون ﴾ بيوسف ويبغون له الغوائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Most people” may mean humanity generally or specifically the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: أراد العموم أو أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if Muhammad exerted every possible effort, those addressed would not believe.
rows.anchor: وما هم بمؤمنين ولواجتهدت كل الاجتهاد على إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object for which Muhammad asks no payment may be his delivering the message or the Quran itself.
rows.anchor: عن التبليغ أو على القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a reminder and admonition from God.
rows.anchor: ما هو الا عظة من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through a messenger, the reminder urges all people to seek salvation.
rows.anchor: وحث على طلب النجاة على لسان رسول من رسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are indications of the Creator, His attributes, and His oneness; people pass by or see the signs on earth yet turn away from considering them.
rows.anchor: من علامة ودلالة على الخالق وعلى صفاته وتوحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended signs include traces of destroyed peoples and other instructive lessons.
rows.anchor: المراد ما يرون من آثار الأمم الهالكة وغير ذلك من العبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people affirm God as their creator and the creator of the heavens and earth, but still worship idols; in severe trouble they call on God while continuing to associate others with Him.
rows.anchor: في إقراره بالله وبأنه خلقه وخلق السموات والأرض إلا وهو مشرك بعبادة الوثن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority explanation is that the verse concerns polytheists who acknowledge God yet associate others with Him.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على أنها نزلت في المشركين لأنهم مقرون بالله خالقهم ورازقهم

rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: The Qadariyya's attribution of creative power to human beings is counted as a form of associationism.
rows.anchor: ومن جملة الشرك ما يقوله القدرية من اثبات قدرة التخليق للعبد

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: The author identifies the Sunnis' position—that none creates but God—as pure monotheism.
rows.anchor: والتوحيد المحض ما يقوله أهل السنة وهو انه لا خالق الا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ghāshiya is a punishment that envelops and encompasses people.
rows.anchor: عقوبة تغشاهم وتشملهم ﴿ من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة ﴾ القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour may come suddenly while people are unaware that it is arriving.
rows.anchor: القيامة ﴿ بغتة ﴾ حال أي فجأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's path is calling people to faith and God's oneness; sabīl, “path,” can be either masculine or feminine in Arabic.
rows.anchor: هذه السبيل التي هي الدعوة إلى الإيمان والتوحيد سبيلي والسبيل والطريق يذكران ويؤنثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling to God “upon insight” means inviting people to His religion with clear proof, not blindly.
rows.anchor: ادعو إلى دينه مع حجة واضحة غير عمياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing treats “I” as emphasis for the implicit subject of “I call,” with “those who follow me” coordinated: both the Prophet and his followers call to God's path.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنا ﴾ تأكيد للمستتر فى ادعو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes “I” a new subject, with the fronted phrase “upon insight” as its predicate; “those who follow me” is coordinated with “I,” so both stand on proof.
rows.anchor: أنا مبتدأ وعلى بصيرة خبر مقدم ومن اتبعنى عطف على أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of God's transcendence disavows partners, and Muhammad declares that he is not among those who associate others with God.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وسبحان الله ﴾ وانزهه عن الشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent human men, not angels, since opponents had asked why God did not send angels; the wording also excludes women from prophethood.
rows.anchor: لا ملائكة لأنهم كانوا يقولون لو شاء ربنا لأنزل ملائكة أو ليست فيهم امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers were from towns because town dwellers are more knowledgeable and discerning, while Bedouins are ignorant and coarse.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أعلم وأحلم وأهل البوادى فيهم الجهل والجفاء

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads the verb “We reveal” with the letter nūn.
rows.anchor: ﴿ نوحي ﴾ بالنون حفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “abode of the Hereafter” means the abode of the final Hour and is better for those who avoid associating partners and believe in God.
rows.anchor: الآخرة أي ولدار الساعة الآخرة

rows.speaker: مكى وأبو عمرو وحمزة وعلى
rows.claim: Makkī, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and ʿAlī read the final verb with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبالياء مكى وابو عمرو وحمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers became despairing of their people's faith.
rows.anchor: يئسوا من إيمان القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the doubled reading, the messengers became certain their people had denied them.
rows.anchor: وأيقن الرسل أن قومهم كذبوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the Kufan light reading, the messengers thought those addressed had been given a false promise or that the messengers had failed to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: وبالتخفيف كوفي أي وظن المرسل اليهم أن الرسل قد كذبوا أي أخلفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the people thought the messengers had lied about being victorious over them.
rows.anchor: أي كذبتهم الرسل في انهم ينصرون عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's aid came suddenly and unexpectedly for the prophets and their believers.
rows.anchor: للأنبياء والمؤمنين بهم فجأة من غير احتساب

rows.speaker: الشامي وعاصم
rows.claim: Al-Shāmī and ʿĀṣim read fanajji with one nūn, a doubled jīm, and a fatḥa on yāʾ, as a past passive verb.
rows.anchor: بنون واحدة وتشديد الجيم وفتح الياء شامى وعاصم على لفظ الماضي المبنى للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use two nūns, the second hidden before jīm, and a vowelless yāʾ.
rows.anchor: من الباقون فنجى بنونين ثانيتهما ساكنة مخفاة للجيم بعدها واسكان الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those saved are the prophet and whoever believed in him.
rows.anchor: اي النبي ومن آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's might cannot be turned away from criminal disbelievers.
rows.anchor: عذابنا ﴿ عن القوم المجرمين ﴾ الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stories that teach a lesson may be the accounts of the prophets and their peoples or specifically Joseph and his brothers.
rows.anchor: اي في قصص الأنبياء وأممهم أو في قصة يوسف وأخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's fortunes moved from affection to the pit, then from a prison bed to the throne; patience ended in safety and honor, while plotting ended in shame and regret.
rows.anchor: من غاية الحب إلى غيابة الجب ومن الحصير إلى السرير فصارت عاقبة الصبر سلامة وكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is not fabricated, contrary to the disbelievers' claim, but confirms the earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: ولكن تصديق الكتب التي تقدمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran details what religion requires because Sunnah, consensus, and analogy rely on it as their governing basis.
rows.anchor: يحتاج إليه في الدين لأنه القانون الذي تستند إليه السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For believers in God and His prophets, the Quran guides away from error and saves from punishment.
rows.anchor: لقوم يؤمنون ﴾ بالله وانبيائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase after “but” is coordinated with the predicate of “was” in the grammatical construction.
rows.anchor: وما نصب بعد لكن معطوف على خبر كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted report urges teaching Surat Yusuf to slaves and household members; it says this eases death agonies and gives strength not to envy a Muslim.
rows.anchor: علموا ارقاءكم سورة يوسف فايما عبد تلاها وعلمها أهله وما ملكت يمينه هون الله عليه سكرات الموت

rows.speaker: أبو منصور
rows.claim: Abu Mansur says Joseph's story consoles Muhammad: Joseph endured his brothers' scheming despite shared faith and kinship, so Muhammad should all the more endure Quraysh's harm despite religious disagreement.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو منصور رحمه الله في ذكر قصة يوسف عليه السلام واخوته تصبير لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says every book God revealed contained the complete Surah Yusuf just as it appears in the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب إن الله تعالى لم ينزل كتابا إلا وفيه سورة يوسف عليه السلام تامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥān is a verbal noun meaning God's transcendence from evil; it is accusative after an omitted verb, then functions in place of that verb to express emphatic transcendence.
rows.anchor: تنزيه الله عن السوء وهو علم للتسبيح كعثمان للرجل وانتصابه بفعل مضمر متروك إظهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asrā and sarā are two Arabic forms with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وسرى وأسرى لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laylan is an adverb; since a night journey already implies night, its explicit mention either emphasizes this or signals that only part of the night was needed for a forty-night journey from Mecca to Syria.
rows.anchor: نصب على الظرف وقيده بالليل والاسراء لا يكون إلا بالليل للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report places the starting point at Umm Haniʾ's house; “the Sacred Mosque” can refer to the surrounding sanctuary because it encloses and is associated with the mosque.
rows.anchor: قيل أسرى به من دار أم هانىء بنت أبي طالب والمراد بالمسجد الحرام الحرم لاحاطته بالمسجد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the whole sanctuary counts as a mosque.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما الحرم كله مسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that the journey began at the Sacred Mosque itself.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو المسجد الحرام بعينه وهوالظاهر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said Gabriel brought the Buraq while he was at the Sacred Mosque, between sleep and wakefulness, and that he was taken up to heaven that night.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام بينما انا في المسجد الحرام في ال عند البيت بين النائم واليقظان إذ أتانى جبريل بالبراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent began from Jerusalem; the Prophet told Quraysh about their caravan's number of camels and condition, heavenly wonders, meeting prophets, and reaching the Frequented House and the Lote Tree.
rows.anchor: وكان العروج به من بيت المقدس وقد أخبر قريشا عن عيرهم وعدد جمالها وأحوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey occurred a year before the Hijra while the Prophet was awake.
rows.anchor: وكان الاسراء قبل الهجرة بسنة وكان في اليقظة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha swore that Muhammad's body was not missing and said only his soul ascended; a similar report is attributed to Muʿāwiya.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت والله ما فقد جسد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority hold that the Prophet ascended bodily while awake, since a dreamer has no special merit or distinction.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأول الجمهور إذ لا فضيلة للحالم ولا مزية للنائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Masjid al-Aqṣā is Jerusalem, for no mosque lay beyond it at that time.
rows.anchor: هو بيت المقدس لأنه لم يكن حينئذ وراءه مسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding land is blessed with religious and worldly blessings: prophets worshiped there, revelation descended there, and rivers and fruit trees surround it.
rows.anchor: يريد بركات الدين والدنيا لأنه متعبد الأنبياء عليهم السلام ومهبط الوحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Muhammad signs of divine oneness and his prophethood through the signs he saw in the heavens.
rows.anchor: الدالة على وحدانية الله وصدق نبوته وبرؤيته السموات وما فيها من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears speech and sees deeds.
rows.anchor: السميع ﴾ للاقوال ﴿ البصير ﴾ بالافعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person narration to first-person plural and back is iltifāt, a rhetorical form of eloquence.
rows.anchor: ثم باركنا ثم أنه هو وهي طريقة الالتفات التي هي من طريق البلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book given to Moses is the Torah, made guidance for the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: وجعلناه ﴾ أي الكتاب وهو التوارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That you should not take” can be parsed as a prohibition or as “lest they take,” with the latter read by Abu ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: أي لا تتخذوا وبالياء أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wakīl is a lord to whom people entrust their affairs instead of God.
rows.anchor: وكيلا ﴾ ربا تكلون اليه أموركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Descendants of those We carried” is accusative as a specification; with the yāʾ reading of the prohibition, it can instead be a vocative addressed to them.
rows.anchor: نصب على الاختصاص أو على النداء فيمن قرأ لا تتخذوا بالياء على النهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was grateful in prosperity and adversity; gratitude answers a blessing by praising its giver.
rows.anchor: في السراء والضراء والشكر مقابلة النعمة بالثناء على المنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Noah would not eat, drink, or dress without saying “Praise be to God.”
rows.anchor: وروى انه كان لا يأكل ولا يشرب ولا يلبس الا قال الحمد لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Children of Israel descend from those who believed in Noah and were carried with him, so they should imitate Noah as their ancestors did.
rows.anchor: وأنتم ذرية من آمن به وحمل معه فاجعلوه اسوتكم كما جعله آباؤكم اسوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sign that children are rightly guided is that they follow their ancestors' practice; the ancestors' earlier conduct is already known.
rows.anchor: وآية رشد الابناء صحة الاقتداء بسنة الآباء وقد عرفتم حال الآباء هنالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave the Children of Israel an irrevocable revelation that they would certainly corrupt the land; the book means the Torah.
rows.anchor: وأوحينا اليهم وحيا مقضيا أي مقطوعا مبتوتا بأنهم يفسدون في الأرض لا محالة والكتاب التوارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic prediction may answer an omitted oath, or the irrevocable decree may function like an oath and govern the verb.
rows.anchor: ولتفسدن جواب قسم محذوف أو جرى القضاء المبتوت مجرى القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first corruption was killing Zechariah and imprisoning Jeremiah after he warned them of God's displeasure; the second was killing John son of Zechariah and attempting to kill Jesus.
rows.anchor: اولاهما قتل زكرياء عليه السلام وحبس أرمياء عليه السلام حين أنذرهم سخط الله والأخرى قتل يحيى بن زكرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their great arrogance means becoming proud of disobeying God, like Pharaoh's arrogance; it refers to oppression and wrong, with corrupt people prevailing over reformers.
rows.anchor: ولتستكبرن عن طاعة الله من قوله أن فرعون علا في الأرض والمراد به البغى والظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the first punishment was due, God empowered servants over Israel who were fierce fighters.
rows.anchor: وعد أولاهما ﴾ أي وعد عقاب أولاهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attackers are variously identified as Sennacherib and his army, Nebuchadnezzar, or Goliath.
rows.anchor: يعنى سنجاريب وجنوده أو بختنصر أو جالوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They killed Israel's scholars, burned the Torah, destroyed the Temple, and took seventy thousand captives.
rows.anchor: قتلوا علماءهم وأحرقوا التوارة وخربوا المسجد وسبوا منهم سبعين ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāsū means they moved through the homes to raid them; al-Zajjāj explains the word as searching for something exhaustively.
rows.anchor: ترددوا للغارة فيها قال الزجاج الجوس طلب الشيء بالاستقصاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised punishment was carried out.
rows.anchor: وكان وعدا مفعولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God restored Israel's dominance after they repented and turned back from corruption and arrogance.
rows.anchor: لكم الكرة ﴾ أي الدولة والغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the restored victory as killing Nebuchadnezzar, rescuing Israelite captives and possessions, and restoring their kingship.
rows.anchor: قيل هي قتل بختنصر واستنقاذ بنى اسرائيل أسراهم وأموالهم ورجوع الملك اليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says their power returned under Saul, when David killed Goliath.
rows.anchor: وقيل أعدنا لكم الدولة بملك طالوت وقتل داود جالوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increased their wealth, sons, and fighting force beyond what they had before.
rows.anchor: وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا ﴾ مما كنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafīr is a collective noun for the group of a man’s people who go out with him.
rows.anchor: تمييز جمع نفر وهو من ينفر مع الرجل من قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the lām in “for yourselves” to mean “against yourselves,” by analogy with the wording of 2:286.
rows.anchor: قيل اللام بمعنى على كقوله وعليها ما اكتسبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the lām retains its ordinary meaning of belonging: each person's good or bad deed and its consequence belong to that person and do not pass to another.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنها على بابها لأن اللام للاختصاص والعامل مختص بجزاء عمله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reportedly said he had neither done good nor evil to anyone, then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن على رضي الله عنه ما أحسنت إلى أحد ولا أسأت اليه وتلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second promised punishment means God empowered the attackers over Israel again.
rows.anchor: وعد المرة الآخرة بعثناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-yasūʾū means that the attackers make the Israelites' faces show sorrow and humiliation; its subject is omitted because the attackers were mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: وحذف لدلالة ذكره أولا عليه أي ليجعلوها بادية آثار المساءة

rows.speaker: الشامي وحمزة وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Shāmī, Ḥamza, and Abū Bakr read the verb in the singular, “to make it sad.”
rows.anchor: ليسوء شامى وحمزة وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the singular reading, the subject can be God, the promise, or the dispatch of the attackers; another reading has God say “that We may make sad.”
rows.anchor: والضمير لله عز وجل أو للوعد أو للبعث لنسوء على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosque they enter is Jerusalem's Temple, as they entered it the first time; they utterly destroy what they conquered or everything for the duration of their domination.
rows.anchor: بيت المقدس ﴿ كما دخلوه أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What they conquered” can be the object of destruction, or the phrase can mean the period of their ascendancy.
rows.anchor: ما علوا مفعول لتبروا أي ليهلكوا كل شيء غلبوه واستولوا عليه أو بمعنى مدة علوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show mercy after the second corruption if Israel repents again and refrains from sin.
rows.anchor: بعد المرة الثانية ان تبتم توبة اخرى وانزجرتم عن المعاصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they return to corruption a third time, God will return to punishing them.
rows.anchor: مرة ثالثة ﴿ عدنا ﴾ إلى عقوبتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did return, so God punished them by setting the Persians over them and imposing tribute.
rows.anchor: وقد عادوا فأعاد الله عليهم النقمة بتسليط الأكاسرة وضرب الأتاوة عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says believers will rule over the Children of Israel until the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما سلط عليهم المؤمنون إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥaṣīr is a place of confinement; prison is called both muḥṣar and ḥaṣīr.
rows.anchor: محبسا يقال للسجن محصر وحصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran guides to the most upright state: worshiping God alone, believing His messengers, and obeying Him.
rows.anchor: وهي توحيد الله والايمان برسله والعمل بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The most upright” may instead mean the religion, community, or path.
rows.anchor: أو للملة أو للطريقة

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: Ḥamza and ʿAlī have a distinct reading for “and gives good news.”
rows.anchor: ويبشر حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great reward promised to believers who do good is Paradise.
rows.anchor: أجرا كبيرا ﴾ أي الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We prepared” means “We readied”; the tāʾ of the form changes to dāl.
rows.anchor: أعتدنا ﴾ أي أعددنا قلبت تاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The painful punishment is the Fire.
rows.anchor: لهم عذابا أليما ﴾ يعنى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse challenges the doctrine of an intermediate status by naming the believers and their reward and the disbelievers and their reward, without naming sinners.
rows.anchor: الآية ترد القول بالمنزلة بين المنزلتين حيث ذكر المؤمنين وجزاءهم والكافرين وجزاءهم ولم يذكر الفسقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person in anger may call for evil against himself, family, property, or children just as he asks good for them; alternatively, he hastily seeks small immediate benefit even at the cost of greater future harm.
rows.anchor: يدعو الله عند غضبه بالشر على نفسه وأهله وماله وولده كما يدعو لهم بالخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are hasty, pursuing whatever enters their minds without the deliberation of a reflective person.
rows.anchor: يتسرع إلى طلب كل ما يقع في قلبه ويخطر بباله لا يأتى فيه تأنى المتبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “the human” means the disbeliever, who mockingly asks for punishment and hastens it as he would ask good when distressed; punishment is certain, so such haste is pointless.
rows.anchor: أو اريد بالإنسان الكافر وأنه يدعوه بالعذاب استهزاء ويستعجل به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the person who invoked punishment as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who challenged that if the message were true God should send the punishment.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هو النصر بن الحرث قال اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the written text, the wāw is omitted from yadʿu to match its spoken form.
rows.anchor: وسقوط الواو من يدع في الخط على موافقة اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes night and day themselves as the two signs, making “night's sign” and “day's sign” explanatory genitives.
rows.anchor: أي الليل والنهار آيتان في أنفسهما فتكون الإضافة في آية الليل وآية النهار للتبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the two signs as the moon and sun: the moon is the sign of night, without rays like the sun, while the radiant sun makes objects clearly visible.
rows.anchor: أو وجعلنا نيرى الليل والنهار آيتيتن يريد الشمس والقمر فمحونا آية الليل التي هي القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daylight lets people pursue their livelihoods.
rows.anchor: لتتوصلوا ببياض النهار إلى التصرف في معايشكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of the two renewed days lets people count years, time limits, and seasons for their work.
rows.anchor: يعنى حساب الآجال ومواسم الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If night and day were alike, people could not distinguish night from day or rest from their labor.
rows.anchor: ولو كانا مثلين لما عرف الليل من النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clearly explained everything people need in religion and worldly life, removing their excuses and leaving no argument against Him.
rows.anchor: بيناه بيانا غير ملتبس فازحنا عللكم وما تركنا لكم حجة علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's ṭāʾir is his deeds, which cling to him like a necklace or shackle that cannot be removed.
rows.anchor: يعنى أن عمله لازم له لزوم القلادة أو الغل للعنق

rows.speaker: الشامي
rows.claim: Al-Shāmī reads “a book that he will meet,” with the clause describing the book.
rows.anchor: يلقاه شامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is spread out when the person meets it, so it is not folded and can be read; alternatively, both clauses describe the book.
rows.anchor: حال من يلقاه يعنى غير مطوى ليمكنه قراءته أو هما صفتان للكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narration continues that God will say to the person to read the book.
rows.anchor: حال من يلقاه يعنى غير مطوى ليمكنه قراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is the record of one's deeds, and every person is resurrected able to read.
rows.anchor: أي كتاب أعمالك وكل يبعث قارئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in “by yourself” is extra, so the phrase means that the self suffices as judge.
rows.anchor: الباء زائده أي كفى نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasīban is an accusative of specification and means an accountant; ʿalayka attaches to it in the construction “he reckoned this against him.”
rows.anchor: تمييز وهو بمعنى حاسب وعلى متعلق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ḥasīban means sufficient, taking the place of a witness, because a witness suffices the claimant regarding what concerns him.
rows.anchor: أو بمعنى الكافى وضع موضع الشهيد فعدى بعلى لأن الشاهد يكفى المدعى ما أهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ḥasīban is masculine because witness, judge, and official roles usually belonged to men; the soul is treated as a man or understood as the person.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر حسيبا لأنه بمنزلة الشهيد والقاضي والأمير إذ الغالب أن يتولى هذه الأمور الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits the guided person, while the consequence of error belongs to the one who strays.
rows.anchor: فلها ثواب الاهتداء وعليها وبال الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every bearer carries only that person's own burden, never another's.
rows.anchor: كل نفس حاملة وزرا فإنما تحمل وزرها لا وزر نفس أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not punish a people with annihilation in this world until sending a messenger who establishes the proof against them.
rows.anchor: وما صح منا أن نعذب قوما عذاب استئصال في الدنيا إلا بعد أن نرسل إليهم رسولا يلزمهم الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “town” here means its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أي أهل قرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to the affluent means God commanded its prosperous and tyrannical leaders to obey; this interpretation is attributed to Abū ʿAmr and al-Zajjāj.
rows.anchor: متنعميها وجبابرتها بالطاعة عن أبي عمرو والزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They then transgressed the command, like the construction “I commanded him, but he disobeyed.”
rows.anchor: أي خرجوا عن الأمر كقولك أمرته فعصى

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads “We made them numerous”; the author supports it with a report describing a blessed wealth as a prolific stallion and a fertile mare.
rows.anchor: أو امرنا كثرنا دليله قراءة يعقوب أمرنا ومنه الحديث خير المال سكة مأبورة ومهرة مأمورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the threat became due, God destroyed the town completely.
rows.anchor: القول ﴾ فوجب عليها الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kam is the object of “We destroyed,” and “of the generations” explains its meaning.
rows.anchor: مفعول ﴿ أهلكنا من القرون ﴾ بيان لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generations after Noah include ʿĀd, Thamūd, and others.
rows.anchor: من بعد نوح ﴾ يعنى عادا وثمود وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is fully informed of His servants' sins even when they conceal them in their hearts, and sees them even when they draw curtains over them.
rows.anchor: خبيرا ﴾ وإن أخفوها في الصدور
